Concurrent DELETE thread: delete_collection -> ShardHolder::stop_gracefully (shard_holder/mod.rs:137) std::mem::take empties the shard map. An in-flight batch query that passed get_collection then executes against the torn-down/rebuilding shard set: select_shards (shard_holder/mod.rs:588, All-selector iterates the emptied map and silently returns Ok(empty)) and the zip-based per-search assembly (query.rs:315-316, zip truncates to the shorter side) can yield an empty/short outer Vec WITHOUT error; the REST batch handler (query_api.rs:167-185) has no result-completeness guard — unlike the single face's .pop() guard at query_api.rs:88-92 which converts the analogous raced outcome to 500 — so the raced condition surfaces as HTTP 200 whose body is not the documented list-of-per-query-results. source_grounding.note: Precise semantics of validation_absent: the static missing-collection validation (get_collection -> NotFound -> 404) EXISTS and demonstrably works (32/40 raced queries got the documented 404, and the no-churn control missing404_001 pinned it exactly); what is absent is (a) race-safety for the lifecycle window after get_collection, and (b) ANY result-completeness validation on the batch REST handler — the one-result-per-search promise of the constraint is never checked at the face that makes the promise, so a raced teardown can answer 200 with a non-conforming body. by_design_in_source is NOT available for the primary observation: neither query_api.rs:167-185 nor query.rs:315-316 carries any intent comment (v3.4 tightened rule: bare unannotated behavior cannot be marked by_design). The SECONDARY (post-cycle by-id) observation IS by-design in source with explicit intent evidence (collection_query.rs:704-705 comment + exclude_referenced_ids doc comment at 525) and is recorded as script-oracle mis-expectation, not a defect signal — the auditor should weigh the verdict accordingly (the it34 race line alone carries DEFECT_FOUND).
